headline: Highest risk is data leakage: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded/app files and send content to OpenAI, while Chatwoot handles customer data and broad egress can expose it if bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files and clipboard, and Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports. If Chatwoot content is copied into ChatGPT or shared via files, prompt injection becomes plausible in default workflows. No shared host channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is copied into ChatGPT Desktop via clipboard or files
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to follow instructions embedded in customer messages or reports
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy for support text
Strip instructions from pasted customer content
Review ChatGPT outputs before reuse in Chatwoot
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files and files from supported macOS apps, and its network egress is vendor-only to api.openai.com. Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders. If customer records are moved into ChatGPT for analysis, sensitive data can leave the support system and reach a third-party backend.
conditions: IF customer data, orders, or interaction history are pasted or uploaded into ChatGPT Desktop
IF Chatwoot exports are opened in supported macOS apps that ChatGPT Desktop can read
mitigations: Avoid sending customer records to ChatGPT Desktop
Redact identifiers before analysis
Use synthetic samples for debugging
Restrict file sharing from support exports
requires-engineering: route sensitive workflows to a local-only model

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while Chatwoot exposes broad API integrations but no local write surface is shown. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The main overlap is read/egress, not competing mutation of the same resource.
conditions: IF Chatwoot is connected to mutable external systems through its listed integrations
IF ChatGPT Desktop is only used for read-only analysis
mitigations: Keep ChatGPT Desktop in read-only workflows
Do not let both agents edit the same external record
Use a single system of record for support actions

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can generate analyses from files and app context, and Chatwoot can act on support workflows and integrations. If Chatwoot operators treat ChatGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into customer-facing actions. The pair lacks a documented verification gate, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop output is pasted into Chatwoot replies, tags, or workflows without review
IF Chatwoot integrations execute actions based on ChatGPT-generated summaries
mitigations: Require human review before sending support actions
Mark AI-generated text clearly in Chatwoot
Cross-check facts against source tickets
requires-engineering: add validation rules for AI-derived fields

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and app content, while Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history. If regulated customer data is moved from Chatwoot into ChatGPT Desktop, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific legal mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from Chatwoot is transferred into ChatGPT Desktop
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the transferred records
mitigations: Classify data before sharing
Exclude regulated records from AI workflows
Document retention expectations for support exports
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across systems
